sci-repo-y7-aran-2015-bio-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Describe a decomposer organism.
options: An animal that eats another animal
A plant that loses its leaves in winter
An organism that lives on Dead and decaying matter.
An animal that uses sound as its main method of communication
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead organic matter, recycling nutrients.

questions.prompt: Identify the biotic factor in an animals environment that can affect its survival.
options: Events such as fire and flood
Competition from other animals for food.
questions.explanation: Competition involving other animals is biotic; water/air are abiotic.

questions.prompt: Why do scientists use scientific names to name living organism?
options: To make communication of scientific information with other scientists easier.
To avoid confusion about which living organism is being studied.
Because Latin is an easy language to learn.
questions.explanation: Both communication and avoiding ambiguity are reasons for scientific naming.

questions.prompt: Which of the following organisms are in the same species? Canis familiaris Canis aureus Vulpes vulpes Sciurus vulgaris
options: None are in the same species.
questions.explanation: No two listed binomials name the same species; shared genus alone is insufficient.

questions.prompt: Which of the following will have the greatest number of different living organisms in it?
questions.explanation: Kingdom is broader than phylum, order or genus in the stated hierarchy.

questions.prompt: Define an organism’s habitat.
options: The place where the organism lives
The place where the organism is at a point in time
The place where all the abiotic factors are suited to the organism’s survival
A place where the organism hunts for food
questions.explanation: Habitat is the place an organism lives.

questions.prompt: Define adaptations.
options: Living factors that influence where an organism lives
Non-living factors that influence where an organism lives
Features of an organism that help it survive in its environment
Organisms that inhabit a specific region
questions.explanation: Adaptations are features that improve survival/reproduction in the relevant environment.

questions.prompt: Identify the term that is defined by the following: ‘an interaction between organisms in  which both the organisms benefit from the relationship and neither is harmed’.
questions.explanation: Mutualism benefits both participants.

questions.prompt: Identify the term that is defined by the following: ‘an interaction between two organisms in  which one of them benefits but the other one is not affected’.
questions.explanation: Commensalism benefits one with no appreciable effect on the other.

questions.prompt: A fox is the ______________ which eats a rabbit. The rabbit is the ___________. The two words needed to complete these sentences are:
questions.explanation: A: the fox is carnivorous and the rabbit is prey.

questions.prompt: A tape worm lives in the gut of humans.  It takes nutrients from the humans and can be               harmful.  This is an example of.
questions.explanation: The tapeworm is a parasite and the human its host.

questions.prompt:
Identify the food chain that is part of this food web.
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch42","id":"e88-image1"}]}]
options: Water plant -> tadpole -> trout -> kingfisher -> decomposers
Phytoplankton -> mosquito larvae -> yabby -> silver perch -> pelican ->     decomposers
Water plant -> yabby -> trout -> kingfisher -> decomposers
questions.explanation: C follows the arrows: phytoplankton→mosquito larva→yabby→silver perch→pelican→decomposers.

questions.prompt: Porifera, Arthropods, Molluscs and Cnidarians are all:
questions.explanation: These are animal phyla, using the school-level names; use Arthropoda, Mollusca and Cnidaria formally.

questions.prompt: Describe a decomposer organism.
options: An animal that eats another animal
A plant that loses its leaves in winter
An organism that breaks down organic matter so it is recycled
An animal that uses sound as its main method of communication
questions.explanation: Decomposition recycles organic matter.

questions.prompt: Identify the biotic factor in an organism’s environment that can affect its survival.
options: Events such as fire and flood
questions.explanation: Competitors for living space are a biotic influence.

questions.prompt: Deduce which of these human activities would have a negative impact on a natural  environment.
options: Clearing forests and replacing them with exotic trees
Removing grazing cattle from a natural woodland
questions.explanation: Clearing native forest and replacing it with exotic trees is the intended negative impact. Effects depend on the particular management context.

questions.prompt: Deduce which of these human activities has a positive effect on food webs.
options: Opening up an area of bushland for recreational activities
Removing introduced predators from an area
Overfishing particular fish species causing a decline in numbers
Introducing exotic species, such as rabbits and foxes
questions.explanation: Removing an introduced predator is the intended conservation intervention; outcomes require ecosystem-specific evaluation.

questions.prompt:
The two photographs to the right are of part of a banksia tree showing the fruit that contains the seeds. The pictures show the tree before and after a fire. Deduce the effect of the fire.
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch42","id":"e87-image4-crop-88c99db6"},{"pack":"repo-science-batch42","id":"e87-image5"}]}]
options: The fire burns the tree and fruit, killing the tree and any seeds.
The fruit explodes and the seeds are destroyed.
The fire dries the fruit, which opens, allowing the seeds to come out.
The fire just causes the tree and the fruit to turn black.
questions.explanation: C: the photographed follicles open, releasing seeds. Avoid generalising that every banksia species requires fire.
